title: The Tenants’ Petition
sceneText:
Five people are standing in the courtyard waiting for you to come out. You are in the office when they come.

At the head of them is a man in his sixties, Old Wendt, whom you have seen twice out in the fields. He has a sheet of paper in his hand.

On the paper are the names of five households, and below them five signatures, three of which are marks.

{@wende}“Roofs and a cow shed,” he says. “It was reported last year. Mr Hartmann wrote it down. It should be in the book.”

There is no grievance in it. He is only telling you something he has already checked.

You open the outstanding list kept in the office. It is dated last November, in a neat hand. It was written down, all right; and nothing follows it.

variants.informed:
You know that the five households are not in the same position.

Old Wendt’s roof has leaked for two years, but there are only two of them in the house, so it is still fit to live in.

The common cow shed by the mill has one corner down, so that the whole village’s cattle are packed into the half that is left. Sickness in cattle spreads.

One is an old woman living alone. Her house will not stand through next winter.

The remaining two have the least damage and the most people in them.
variants.uninformed: There are five names on the list. You do not know which household is worst off.
variants.partial_fair:
You say which three will be done, and why.

Old Wendt nods and says the cow shed is certainly the most pressing. One of the men from the other two households opens his mouth, and in the end closes it again.

{@wende}“And the rest?”

You say after the harvest.

{@wende}“Only keep it in mind.”

He leaves the paper on the stone ledge of the porch.
variants.partial_unfair:
You say which three will be done.

For a moment nobody speaks, and then Old Wendt says “Thank you.” He says it more politely than he said anything before.

The paper is left on the stone ledge of the porch, until the wind takes it to the ground.

effects.logEntry: You approved repairs for all five households.

choices.resultText:
Old Wendt takes the paper back, folds it twice and puts it in his pocket.

{@wende}“Thank you.”

They do not stay.

That afternoon there is less talk in the kitchen than usual. Going past, you find Martha talking to two others, and she stops when she sees you.

The last half of what you hear is “… somebody finally.”

choices.text: Do the three that cannot wait

effects.logEntry: You chose three households to do first.

choices.text: After this year’s harvest is in

effects.logEntry: You put the petition off until after the harvest.

choices.resultText:
Old Wendt is silent for a while.

{@wende}“Right,” he says.

He folds the paper up and puts it away, and turns and goes. The other four follow him. Through all of it not one of them says anything more.

The kitchen light went out earlier than usual that night.
